prompt_strategy.value: For the practice round, the other user recommended "tom" and "jerry", which was fairly easy to recall. For the second round, that became a bit more difficult. As it got more complex, we looked at other pieces of the figurines, like the shapes and colors that made them unique.

prompt_strategy.value: We come up with an initial strategy based on colors for round 1; we then tweaked the same strategy, by adding a second letter on round 2; on round3, we decided to make it more simple and use the initial letter only; for the last round, we tried to use the same one letter per word strategy; since colors were not involved and the time to memorize was shorter, mistakes were made only on this round. We asked each other's opinion all along and it felt like a shared strategy; we divided workload in typing too, it come natural.

- How did you decide on your strategy?

prompt_strategy.value: We looked for key differences and patterns across the images. We looked for ways that each image was unique but could also differentiated from its neighbors so that they were easy to identify. For example, we use the color of the hat, the orientation of the hat (left) and the color of the feet, to come up with a simple naming scheme that allowed each image to have unique identifier. This worked for all but the last round where we could not find a way to repeat this process (all images were unique, but there was not a consistent pattern that we could find to uniquely name each so that the ID was easy to recall.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value:
For the first 3 rounds, the bodies of the characters changed. However, the pattern of the colours of their hats, arms and shoes were consistently different. We simply created labels going in a top-down order, describing the colour of their hat, arms and shoes chronologically. So for example, we had "purple black yellow".

We had to change our strategy for the 4th round, where the characters were completely different. We struggled to really come up with any kind of consistent pattern for them. We tried to give ourselves a chance by using a similar system to the first 3 rounds - counting the number of arms and legs showing in each character. There were multiple characters that would've had the same labels, so we introduced a 3rd number to differentiate via memory afterwards. For example, if character1 had 1 leg and 1 arm showing and character2 had 1 leg and 1 arm showing, we would have "1 1 1" and "1 1 2".

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: We decided our strategy based on colors.  For the most part, all of our names were based on the color of the hair, arms and legs.  For the last round It was a bit more challenging and we based them on the shapes, tallest, what they reminded us of, etc....It made it easier to remember the names.  We only changed our strategy for the last game when not all of them had the basic make-up of hair, arms and legs.  So we named on "tallest" as it was the tallest of them all.  It was based on those types of characteristics instead of color.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: none

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: We both basically had the same approach on how to name them.  We thought by going with the color scheme was the best and easiest way to remember.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: For me my strategy was to first identify what the image closely resembled, so looking at identifying characters like a beak for a bird, ears for the owl, dialing  wheel for the phone. Because it is a memory game, I would generalize the identity, so for example if it had a beak, instead of giving a specific bird name like chicken or dove, I would go with bird because it is easier to remember and convince my partner about. I changed my strategy if my partner had a better idea, that was to recall.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
